newsitem.title: USA: FDA outlines approach on ending CFC sprays.
newsitem.headline: FDA outlines approach on ending CFC sprays.

text.p: Citing new alternatives to ozone-destroying chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) propellants, the Food and Drug Administration Wednesday outlined how it may gradually start phasing out medical products using CFCs.

Only one alternative has been approved so far, and the FDA said it would not phase out any of the CFC propellants, used in inhalants for patients with asthma and other respiratory diseases, until follow-up post-marketing data established that the alternatives work well and are acceptable to patients.

CFC use has been declining in the United States for nearly 20 years, and commercial production and importation has been banned since last year. But essential medical products containing CFC are exempt.

Metered dose inhalers for asthma, emphysemia and other respiratory conditions had used CFC propellants. But the FDA said last August it had approved the first non CFC-propellant inhaler, and others are likely to become available.
FDA officials said there was no timetable for the phase-out under the rules it proposed Wednesday, which are subject to a 60-day public comment period.
